appraisal_events.evidence: cet homme important qui allait user en ma faveur du grand prestige qu'il devait avoir aux yeux de Mme Swann m'inspira subitement une tendresse si grande que j'eus peine à me retenir de ne pas embrasser ses douces mains blanches et fripées
appraisal_events.explanation: The young narrator's admiration for Norpois surges because Norpois promises to use his supposed prestige with Mme Swann on the narrator's behalf; the older narrating voice frames this near-worshipful reaction (comparing himself to an Olympian god and to a criminal revising testimony) with gentle irony, so the elevation is presented but not fully endorsed.

appraisal_events.evidence: on me raconta qu'il avait fait allusion à une soirée d'autrefois dans laquelle il avait « vu le moment où j'allais lui baiser les mains », je ne rougis pas seulement jusqu'aux oreilles, je fus stupéfait
appraisal_events.explanation: Years later the narrator learns that Norpois turned his private, near-worshipful gesture into an anecdote recounted to others, exposing him retrospectively and provoking a strong blush and stupefaction.

status_effects.explanation: In the narrator's local perception Norpois is elevated by his promised influence and prestige with Mme Swann, though the irony of the framing keeps the elevation from being fully clear-cut.
The narrator is embarrassed and exposed when he discovers his private display of devotion had been retained and retold by Norpois as social anecdote, deflating his assumed privacy and dignity.

ambiguities: The passage moves into a long philosophical digression on memory and forgetting; whether the closing anecdote about Norpois's retelling is primarily an evaluative diminishment of the narrator or a neutral illustration of memory's surprises is not fully certain.

The report of Norpois's remark reaches the narrator secondhand ('on me raconta'), so it is uncertain whether Norpois himself should be read as the direct evaluative source or merely the originator within a layered chain of social reporting.
